The test image shows close-up soybean stems/petioles with pronounced dark brown to reddish-brown/purple discoloration running along them. Green pods visible in background. No obvious white mold or visible fungal fruiting bodies at this magnification.

Key features: stem/petiole discoloration, dark brown-purple elongated lesions on stems, hairy stem surface still intact.

Let me check reference images for the top candidates: Anthracnose, Diaporthe, Phytophthora, and a few others.
Those don't match. Let me now look at a few more candidates more closely.
Let me look more carefully at a few more references to confirm.

I've now viewed 14 reference images. Let me consolidate my analysis.

**Test image observations:**
- Affected part: stem/petiole junction at a node
- Color: dark brownish-purple to reddish-brown discoloration running the length of the stem/petiole
- Green pods visible and attached (mid-to-late season)
- Hairy (pubescent) stem surface intact
- No white mold, no yellow leaf spots, no obvious black pycnidia rows
- The petiole shows a slightly bent/curved shape (possible shepherd's crook)

**Differential reasoning:**
- **Anthracnose**: "Red to brown dark irregular lesions on stems, pods, and petioles; affected petioles may show a shepherd's crook appearance" — matches the elongated reddish-brown petiole discoloration and the bent shape at the node
- **Diaporthe**: Requires linear rows of black pycnidia — not clearly visible
- **Cercospora/Purple_Seed_Stain**: Primarily leaf/seed symptoms, doesn't match stem focus
- **Phytophthora/Charcoal_Rot/Brown_Stem_Rot**: Internal stem discoloration, wilted plants — test image shows live plant with green pods

The close-up view of a dark reddish-brown petiole with shepherd's crook tendency near a node with green pods is the hallmark presentation of Anthracnose.

No white mold, no linear pycnidia rows (Diaporthe), and no systemic root/pith involvement (BSR/SDS). The color and location are most consistent with Anthracnose stem and petiole infection."}
